chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: The missed option and Latimore's settlement
summary: A contract refusal arrived a day late, and Latimore won a large payment from the company but offered the musicians far less; Cook and most of the band were unhappy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So, okay, so you were for six months at this --

After six months contract there was a mistake between the managing-director, that is Mr. Andre Charlot. There were two, Andre Charlot, Ecout de Mobile. There were two associations. And there were mistakes that Mr. Latimore expected an option on a contract. And we all thought that action was okay, because we had no news, but it happened that the refusal came one day late. (Laughter).
And Mr. Latimore, who was a wonderful businessman, took advantage of that.
And he attacked the company, and he got that much money. That much money Well, that's happened --
He got a lot, a lot more money out.
Not only that, what he offered us, was nothing in comparison to what we should have gotten, you see.

With the sums that he -- and Dad Cook was not satisfied, and the majority of the members were not satisfied. I, being the youngest, I was not satisfied, either. But I was following the majority, you see.
And, Latimore, with all that money he just figured if they don't
give in, I don't know, send to America and get some other musicians, and artists --
